title: The Matrix Inverse as a Polynomial over a Commutative Ring
description: Removes the field hypothesis from the parent inverse-as-polynomial result: for a matrix A over an arbitrary commutative ring R with IsUnit (det A), the inverse is the evaluation at A of an explicit polynomial, A⁻¹ = (aeval A) r with r = C (Ring.inverse (−c₀)) · divX (charpoly A) of degree < n. Over a general ring det A ≠ 0 no longer suffices — one needs det A to be an actual unit — and the field division (−c₀)⁻¹ is replaced by Ring.inverse (−c₀). The witnessing non-field case is R = ℤ: a matrix in GL(n, ℤ) (det = ±1) has an integer-coefficient polynomial inverse, out of reach of the field-only parent.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)

mathlibDependencies.description: The Cayley–Hamilton theorem: a matrix is a root of its own characteristic polynomial, aeval A (charpoly A) = 0, over any commutative ring
det A = (−1)ⁿ · (charpoly A).coeff 0, the identity relating the determinant to the constant term of the characteristic polynomial; used to promote IsUnit (det A) to IsUnit (−c₀)
Splitting off the constant term: divX p * X + C (p.coeff 0) = p
Ring.inverse u * u = 1 for a unit u; the commutative-ring replacement for field division by the unit −c₀
Promotion of a left inverse to the nonsingular inverse and the commutativity of one-sided matrix inverses over a commutative ring
A⁻¹ = Ring.inverse (det A) • adjugate A, reconciling the polynomial inverse with Mathlib's adjugate formula
Algebra.adjoin R {x} equals the range of aeval x; used to place A⁻¹ inside the subalgebra R[A]
The characteristic polynomial is monic of degree Fintype.card n, giving the degree bookkeeping for the < n bound

originalContributions: invPoly A: the inverse polynomial r = C (Ring.inverse (−c₀)) · divX (charpoly A) over an arbitrary commutative ring, whose evaluation at A is A⁻¹

isUnit_neg_charpoly_coeff_zero: the unit lens — IsUnit (det A) forces IsUnit (−c₀), via det A = (−1)ⁿ c₀ and the fact that (−1)ⁿ is a self-inverse unit; this is where det ≠ 0 is genuinely strengthened to det being a unit
aeval_divX_mul_self: the additive form of Cayley–Hamilton, (divX p)(A)·A + c₀•1 = 0, valid over any commutative ring
aeval_invPoly_mul_self: the ring-theoretic left-inverse identity, with the field division (−c₀)⁻¹·(−c₀)=1 replaced by Ring.inverse_mul_cancel on the unit −c₀
inv_eq_aeval_invPoly: the main result A⁻¹ = (aeval A) (invPoly A) over a commutative ring
invPoly_natDegree_lt: the degree bound deg(invPoly A) < n = Fintype.card n
inv_mem_adjoin: A⁻¹ ∈ Algebra.adjoin R {A}, i.e. the inverse lies in the subalgebra R[A]
self_mul_aeval_invPoly / exists_inv_eq_aeval: the right-inverse companion and the packaged degree-bounded existence statement
inv_eq_smul_adjugate: reconciliation with Mathlib's Ring.inverse (det A) • adjugate A
GL(n, ℤ) instance: over ℤ (not a field) any integer matrix with unit determinant has its inverse in the integer subalgebra ℤ[A]

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. #print axioms reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for all nine theorems. The matrix is assumed to have a unit determinant (IsUnit (det A)) over a commutative ring; the degree-bound and packaged-existence theorems additionally assume Nontrivial R and Nonempty n. Built on Mathlib's Cayley–Hamilton theorem and nonsingular-inverse theory.

overview.historicalContext: The parent result expresses the inverse of an invertible matrix over a field as a polynomial in the matrix, of degree below n, using the Cayley–Hamilton division trick. Over a general commutative ring the two notions that coincide over a field — the determinant being nonzero and the matrix being invertible — split apart: a matrix over ℤ is invertible in Mₙ(ℤ) exactly when its determinant is a unit (±1), not merely nonzero. This entry carries the same explicit construction through over an arbitrary commutative ring, assuming precisely IsUnit (det A), and replaces the scalar division (−c₀)⁻¹ by the ring inverse Ring.inverse (−c₀). The payoff is genuinely beyond the field case: over ℤ it exhibits the inverse of a unimodular matrix as an integer-coefficient polynomial in the matrix.
overview.problemStatement: Remove the field hypothesis from the inverse-as-polynomial result: show that for a matrix A over a commutative ring R with IsUnit (det A), the inverse is A⁻¹ = (aeval A) r for an explicit r = C (Ring.inverse (−c₀)) · divX (charpoly A) with deg r < n, and that A⁻¹ ∈ R[A].
overview.text: Let p = charpoly A and c₀ = p.coeff 0. Cayley–Hamilton gives p(A) = 0; writing p = divX(p)·X + C c₀ and evaluating at A yields (divX p)(A)·A + c₀•1 = 0, i.e. (divX p)(A)·A = (−c₀)•1. Since det A = (−1)ⁿ c₀ and det A is a unit, −c₀ is a unit, so multiplying by Ring.inverse (−c₀) gives A⁻¹ = Ring.inverse (−c₀) • (divX p)(A) = (aeval A) r with r = C (Ring.inverse (−c₀)) · divX p, of degree < deg p = n.
overview.proofStrategy: The crux is isUnit_neg_charpoly_coeff_zero: from det A = (−1)ⁿ c₀ (Matrix.det_eq_sign_charpoly_coeff) and the fact that (−1)ⁿ squares to 1 (hence is a unit), IsUnit (det A) gives IsUnit c₀ and thus IsUnit (−c₀). The additive Cayley–Hamilton identity aeval_divX_mul_self comes from divX_mul_X_add and Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly. Dividing by the unit −c₀ via Ring.inverse_mul_cancel produces a left inverse that is a polynomial in A; Matrix.inv_eq_left_inv promotes it to A⁻¹ and Matrix.mul_eq_one_comm gives the right-inverse companion. The degree bound combines natDegree_C_mul_le with degree_divX_lt and charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim; membership in R[A] uses Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval.
keyInsights: Over a commutative ring, invertibility of A is IsUnit (det A), strictly stronger than det A ≠ 0 — this is the exact hypothesis the construction needs
The field division (−c₀)⁻¹ is replaced by Ring.inverse (−c₀), and the unit status of −c₀ is inherited from det A = (−1)ⁿ c₀
(−1)ⁿ is its own inverse, so it is always a unit; the unit-ness of c₀ therefore transfers to and from det A with no extra hypotheses
The same explicit polynomial r = C (Ring.inverse (−c₀)) · divX (charpoly A) works verbatim over any commutative ring, of degree < n
The witnessing non-field instance is GL(n, ℤ): a unimodular integer matrix has an integer-coefficient polynomial inverse, i.e. A⁻¹ ∈ ℤ[A]

sections.title: Documentation, Setup and the Inverse Polynomial
sections.summary: Header motivating the removal of the field hypothesis (with the GL(n, ℤ) witnessing case), targeted Mathlib imports, setup over a commutative ring R and finite index n, and the definition invPoly A = C (Ring.inverse (−c₀)) · divX (charpoly A).
sections.mathContext: Over a commutative ring the inverse polynomial is built from the ring inverse of the (negated) constant term of the characteristic polynomial, in place of the field reciprocal used by the parent.

sections.title: Invertibility Forces a Unit Constant Term
sections.summary: isUnit_neg_charpoly_coeff_zero: IsUnit (det A) implies IsUnit (−c₀), via det A = (−1)ⁿ c₀ and the self-inverse unit (−1)ⁿ.
sections.mathContext: The exact strengthening of the field condition c₀ ≠ 0: over a ring the negated constant term must be an honest unit so that Ring.inverse (−c₀) is a genuine inverse.

sections.title: Cayley–Hamilton in Additive Form
sections.summary: aeval_divX_mul_self: evaluating charpoly A = divX(charpoly A)·X + C c₀ at A gives (divX p)(A)·A + c₀•1 = 0, over any commutative ring.
sections.mathContext: Peeling off the constant term of the characteristic polynomial isolates the relation (polynomial in A)·A = scalar that produces the inverse.

sections.title: The Inverse as a Polynomial in A
sections.summary: aeval_invPoly_mul_self, inv_eq_aeval_invPoly, invPoly_natDegree_lt, inv_mem_adjoin, self_mul_aeval_invPoly: (aeval A)(invPoly A) is the two-sided inverse of A, of degree < n, lying in the subalgebra R[A].
sections.mathContext: Dividing the additive relation by the unit −c₀ via Ring.inverse_mul_cancel yields a polynomial in A equal to A⁻¹; Matrix.inv_eq_left_inv and mul_eq_one_comm package both sides, and Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval places it in R[A].

sections.title: Packaged Existence, Adjugate Reconciliation and the ℤ Instance
sections.summary: exists_inv_eq_aeval (degree-bounded existence), inv_eq_smul_adjugate (agreement with Mathlib's Ring.inverse (det A) • adjugate A), and the concrete GL(n, ℤ) example placing the inverse of a unimodular integer matrix in ℤ[A].
sections.mathContext: The polynomial inverse coincides with Mathlib's adjugate inverse, and the non-field ℤ instance shows the field-only parent is genuinely extended.

conclusion.summary: The inverse-as-polynomial corollary of Cayley–Hamilton extends from fields to arbitrary commutative rings: for a matrix A with IsUnit (det A), the inverse is the evaluation at A of an explicit polynomial invPoly A = C (Ring.inverse (−c₀)) · divX (charpoly A) of degree < n, and A⁻¹ ∈ R[A]. All 9 theorems and 1 definition are fully verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Assuming det A to be a unit (rather than merely nonzero) is exactly the right hypothesis over a general commutative ring, and the ring inverse Ring.inverse (−c₀) replaces field division cleanly. The concrete consequence is that a unimodular integer matrix has an integer-coefficient polynomial inverse — the inverse lies in ℤ[A] — which the field-only parent cannot express.
openQuestions: Sharpen the degree bound using a minimal-polynomial analogue over a commutative ring, where the minimal polynomial may fail to be well-defined without a field or integral-domain hypothesis.
Characterize the largest class of base rings R for which the same explicit polynomial witnesses A⁻¹ under det A ≠ 0 alone rather than IsUnit (det A).
